subject: Neo.K, dimension_aware_log_physics_stress_bundle.zip (2026-08-10)
scope: exact dimensional algebra, an external anchor for Stefan-Boltzmann, and cancellation-free routes to the hard cases. Not about Collatz.

phase_cell.note: hbar = h/(2 pi) makes (2 pi hbar)^3 = h^3 identically; no pi survives.

stefan_boltzmann.why_this_is_an_external_anchor: k_B, h and c are exact defined constants since the 2019 SI revision, so sigma is exactly determined by the formula and CODATA's digits are an expectation this arm did not author.

lorentz_gamma.note: 1 - beta^2 = (1-beta)(1+beta) removes the cancellation entirely, so gamma needs no log-difference trick at all - only enough precision to hold 1e-40. The bundle's log-diff-exp path gets the same number by a different method, which is what makes the agreement worth something.

assessment.what_it_establishes: the additive-coordinate representation survives contact with real formulas: products become sums, SI dimensions compose as integer vectors, illegal additions are rejected structurally, and severe cancellation is handled at working precision. Every benchmark reproduces its reference value.
assessment.what_it_does_not: nothing about Collatz. This is a representation stress test, and its Collatz relevance is only that item 01 used the same coordinate.
assessment.relation_to_the_line: A branch rather than a continuation. Item 01 applied log coordinates to Collatz; item 02 applies the same coordinate to dimensional physics. The nine-paper series then goes the other way entirely, replacing logarithms with exact affine operators over the integers - Paper 02 §28 says an exact certificate need not depend on a floating logarithm. So this branch is not an ancestor of the series' method; it is the road not taken, and it is worth keeping precisely because it shows the alternative was tried and how far it actually goes.
